template_check.injectivity_argument: Each fixed slot embedding is injective on seven distinct formal variables. Every parity gadget must use all four named variables; rule60/90/150 have different named-main slot supports, so their image sets cannot coincide. Labels of helpers are already part of the subset choice; no extra rule-selector or helper-factorial charge is required.
template_check.description_identity: Helper renamings may expand to isomorphic patterns, yet remain different labelled descriptions. A79 explicitly sums description weights, so quotienting by relabelling is a different weighting.
template_check.count_classification: 504 is the exact count of this Cartesian family of labelled local templates, conditional on the separately audited exhaustive count 168. The frozen census growth code already supplies a valid collision-repair decoder for these gadget embeddings. Conditional on a demonstrated counting property for all three growths, 504 is a lower bound on counting descriptions and mass under this chosen weighting, never an exhaustive counter count. Without the all-depth counting bridge for rule90/150 it is a count of decoded candidate descriptions rather than an unconditional lower bound on proven counters.

description_critique.claim: Astronomically rare / 10^-29 likely / among the rarest
description_critique.finding: Summing a found subset supplies a LOWER bound on total counting mass once descriptions and counting are valid. A tiny lower bound supplies no upper bound; all remaining descriptions could count. No exhaustion or bound on the unexamined counting descriptions is given.

description_critique.claim: The formula is the counter's code length
description_critique.finding: It encodes h, m and an unordered m-subset of labelled local triples, conditional on a fixed growth decoder. The frozen preregistration and census.py ALREADY specify initial width3, growth+1, unrestricted initial mains, one global R, missing=R, terminal NAE closure and equality-copy repairs. Shared decoder conventions can legitimately have zero per-description charge in this chosen language. The required qualification is conditional ideal local-template length under that fixed decoder, not a missing-decoder Block or a shortest description over other languages.

description_critique.claim: All 504 raw templates are valid strict NAE growth descriptions
description_critique.finding: Without copies, only 12 rule60, 12 rule90 and 48 rule150 templates avoid repeated identities within every NAE at the ends. This does NOT invalidate the other compiled descriptions: census.py already supplies the fixed equality-copy convention. A copy adds eight NAE constraints and eight used distinctions, including the copy, so h helpers and m knots per position describe the bulk gadget inventory rather than the full boundary inventory. These additions need not add per-description bits when built into the shared decoder.

description_critique.claim: 104-106 bits are literal binary codeword lengths
description_critique.finding: log2(binomial(...)) is generally fractional. These are exact ideal self-information values for uniform subset selection, not lengths of individual finite binary words. A simple fixed-width rank code uses 106 and 104 bits respectively. Exact uniform choices from fair coins can instead use variable-length rejection; the semantic object's probability is 1/M, but it aggregates multiple coin prefixes.

description_critique.claim: Rule150 needs a fifth parity argument/reference in the interior
description_critique.finding: It does not: the four named parity variables are new i and all three old mains. R remains needed only as the globally shared value for missing old positions; rule60 and rule90 also use R in every interior update. The declared slot set includes all four distinct main slots used by rule150.

The calculation compares two known parity constructions in this selected local-template language. Minimum knot number is not shortest code length across arbitrary descriptions or alternative counting constructions, and h=4 gadgets were not exhaustively counted. The 504 numerator includes h=3 only.

Name the sampling and rejection convention and denominator. Gamma headers plus uniform subsets define a particular subprobability mass when out-of-range m is rejected. Conditioning on accepted descriptions changes shares; neither version is a probability over realities selected by the mathematics.

conclusion_classification.finding: The original S1 m*(f) table for f<=6 and the labelled f=3 family are bounded synthesis data. This lane verifies recovered gadget relations, not optimality. The parent audit reports a new extension proving the unrestricted 'at least 10': remove helpers of degree<=1, then 2f+4<=3m<=27 gives f<=11 for m<=9, and synthesize f=7..11 as UNSAT. This requires integration of that independent parent evidence; it was absent from the original argument. General pp-definability is standard; the exact minima are not supplied by that reference.

Replacing parity by an exact existential definition with disjoint fresh helpers, and faithful collision handling, preserves the named relation by composition. S2 checks wiring. Additive CA algebra is standard. Exact depth life strings are new bounded data for this boundary contract. The stored rule90 and rule150 classes are only 'unexplained' through 64; MOW does not by itself verify this expanding-seed/terminal-NAE satisfiability criterion or prove these growths count.

The two ideal local-template lengths and -96.64199 arithmetic are reproducible conditional on the fixed growth decoder, which already states the growth and collision conventions. They do not establish a shortest description across constructions, total counting probability, rarity upper bound or comparison with other capabilities.

240=12 deletions +12*(31-12) replacements in the declared one-gadget neighbourhood. Minimality alone prevents any deletion from preserving parity; the three parity-preserving replacements and other finite life classes are substantive bounded data, being checked by the other lane. A 1.25% local mutation survival rate is not a global rarity estimate; settling is finite-classifier terminology here.

honesty_and_rhetoric.P3: Honest negative outcome and failed-prediction label; avoid turning a finite observed tail into an all-depth theorem.
honesty_and_rhetoric.rule90_rule150: The words 'count too' outrun the actual 'unexplained within 64' classifier. A separate analytic bridge to the precise boundary/closure predicate is required, rather than citing general additive-CA algebra.
honesty_and_rhetoric.fragility: The finite predeclared result is meaningful in its one-gadget mutation neighbourhood; it does not establish global fine tuning or probability of arithmetic-capable patterns.

primary_sources.title: Martin, Odlyzko and Wolfram, Algebraic Properties of Cellular Automata (1984), author-hosted reprint
primary_sources.verified_locations: Sections 2, 3A, 4A and 4F; reprint pp. 75-77, 90-91, 99-101; PDF pages 5-7, 20, 29-31.
primary_sources.establishes: Additive cellular automata have a polynomial representation; rule 90 uses x+x^-1 and rule 150 uses x+1+x^-1. The paper analyzes finite fixed-size systems, primarily periodic boundaries, and also certain twisted/fixed boundaries.
primary_sources.does_not_establish_in_this_audit: No verified statement for a width-3 seed growing by one position per generation and NAE closure of every consecutive triple of the last generation. The study's exact life bands or nonperiodicity require an explicit transfer/derivation.
primary_sources.authority: Primary paper, background only; not admitted as new proof lineage.

primary_sources.title: Elmar Boehler, Algebraic Closures in Complexity Theory (2005), doctoral dissertation
primary_sources.verified_locations: Definition 3.11 / Proposition 3.12 (p. 37), complementive IN2 discussion (p. 39), Figure 3.5 IN2 row (p. 44; PDF page 44).
primary_sources.establishes: The IN2 co-clone consists of complementive relations and has NAE3 as a base; the displayed alternative base includes EVEN4. The closure corresponds to existential conjunction with equality, allowing variable identification. Thus ordinary pp-definability of EVEN4 from NAE3 is standard.
primary_sources.does_not_establish_in_this_audit: No optimum knot/helper count, enumeration of exact positive strict-distinct gadgets, custom growth boundary result or novelty claim.
primary_sources.authority: Primary author source, background only; not admitted as new proof lineage.
